title: Cartesian degreewise pullback computes the infinity-categorical pullback after Joyal localization
statement: Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories, degreewise pullbacks and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], Cartesian fibrations in the final-horn sense of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and categorical equivalences and the Joyal model structure of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $q:N(\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathrm J})\to\mathcal L$ be a coherent localization at categorical equivalences, in the sense of [def-coef-coherent-localization-interface], and identify $\mathcal L$ with $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ through the derived coherent-nerve comparison of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Let $S,Z$ be small quasicategories, let $p:Z\to S$ be a Cartesian fibration, and let $a:K\to S$ be any small simplicial map. Form $K\times_S Z$ degreewise. Then the image under $q$ of its projection square is a pullback square in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$: the canonical comparison $q(K\times_S Z)\to qK\times_{qS}qZ$ is an equivalence, with its specified projection homotopies. These comparisons are natural in simplicial maps $K\to K\prime$ over $S$. No quasicategory hypothesis on $K$ is imposed; all categories and localization universes may be enlarged together.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.1.4, printed p.206 (PDF p.224), with Proposition 3.3.1.3 and Section 4.2.4 for model/infinity-category comparison. The extracted argument uses Joyal fibrant replacement, the quasicategory fibration characterization and the isofibration pullback theorem. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this theorem.

proof.text: The map $p:Z\to S$ is a Cartesian fibration in the final-horn sense, and the pullback $K\times_S Z$ is degreewise. The relative Cartesian model-structure theorem applies to an arbitrary small simplicial base and an arbitrary map $a:K\to S$; it says that every such degreewise pullback square is a homotopy pullback in the Joyal model structure. Therefore the displayed square is a Joyal homotopy pullback, with no fibrancy assumption on $K$ and with its canonical projections.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.1.4, together with Definition 2.4.1.1; the arbitrary-base pullback formulation is the marked-model expansion used in the project

proof.text: Keep the already fibrant base $S$ fixed. Factor $K\to S$ and $Z\to S$ functorially as trivial cofibrations $i:K\to T$, $j:Z\to E$ followed by Joyal fibrations $T\to S$, $r:E\to S$, using the model-structure node. Since $S$ is fibrant, the composites to the terminal object show that $T,E$ are fibrant, hence quasicategories. Put $H=T\times_S E$. The comparison clause of the relative Cartesian theorem, applied to this fibrant replacement of the cospan, says that the map $h:K\times_S Z\to H$ induced by $i,j$ is a categorical equivalence. The maps $i,j,h$ are consequently sent to equivalences by $q$, since its inverted class is the categorical equivalences. All comparison squares commute strictly before applying $q$.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.1.4 and Section 4.2.4, using the Joyal fibrant replacement

proof.text: The fibrant replacement leg is a Joyal fibration between quasicategories. By the fibration characterization, it has inner-horn lifting and lifts equivalence edges with prescribed source, hence is an isofibration in the sense of the isofibration node. The strict degreewise pullback of any quasicategory along such an isofibration is a pullback in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, by the explicit mapping-space universal property of the isofibration pullback theorem. The coherent-nerve comparison identifies the derived Joyal localization with $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, so the image of the fibrant replacement pullback is a pullback in the chosen localization $\mathcal L$.

Write $P=K\times_S Z$. In the chosen identification with $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, Step 3 gives, for every test object $V$, an equivalence from $\operatorname{Map}(V,qH)$ to the space of pairs of maps $V\to qT$, $V\to qE$ with a specified homotopy between their composites to $qS$. Postcomposition with $qi,qj$ identifies the corresponding cone space for $(qK,qZ)$ with this space: postcomposition with inverse equivalences gives an inverse on both maps and their homotopy; the inverse homotopies are the whiskered inverse equations. Likewise postcomposition with $qh$ identifies $\operatorname{Map}(V,qP)$ with $\operatorname{Map}(V,qH)$. By the commuting squares of Step 2 these identifications carry the cone map for $qP$ to that for $qH$. Thus the cone map for $qP$ is an equivalence for every $V$, proving the pullback criterion. Its homotopy is the image under $q$ of the original strict commuting square, so the resulting equivalence is the canonical comparison with the specified projections.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.1.4, universal mapping-space formulation and naturality

proof.text: For a map $u:K\to K\prime$ over $S$, degreewise pullback gives a map of projection squares with upper map $(u,1_Z)$. Applying the functor $q$ gives a map of their specified cones. The two composites from $q(K\times_S Z)$ to $qK\prime\times_{qS}qZ$ therefore have the same cone: their projections are $qu$ after the $K$-projection and the unchanged $Z$-projection, with the commuting homotopy supplied by this map of squares. The pullback mapping-space equivalence identifies the space of comparisons with this fixed cone with a contractible homotopy fiber. This supplies the commuting homotopy and all its coherent compatibilities for composites and higher simplices of maps over $S$. Consequently the canonical comparisons form a natural equivalence in simplicial maps over $S$.

source.place: Agent consequence of the mapping-space pullback universal property; naturality of the projection square, supplementary to HTT Corollary 3.3.1.4
